bull.b: Record leasing activity demonstrates strong customer demand for Digital Realty’s data center capacity and connectivity services. Growth across hyperscale, colocation, interconnection and AI workloads broadens the revenue base and supports sustained utilization over the next several quarters.

The record backlog provides multi-year visibility into future revenue, while higher occupancy and lower churn indicate improving customer retention and asset utilization. These trends support durable cash NOI growth and reduce reliance on continuously securing entirely new demand.

A broad global footprint, large customer ecosystem and expanding liquid-cooling capability position Digital Realty to serve increasingly complex AI deployments. This infrastructure breadth can deepen customer relationships and support demand as workloads spread across regions and use cases.

bear.b: Sharp free-cash-flow volatility reduces the cash available for dividends, debt reduction and internally funded development. Although operating cash flow remains positive, weaker conversion and heavy investment requirements can constrain financial flexibility when expansion needs are elevated.

Uneven revenue growth and a sharp gross-margin decline indicate that earnings are not compounding consistently. If direct costs or mix pressure persist, the company may generate less profit from each dollar of revenue, limiting operating leverage despite healthy demand.

Data center expansion depends on timely development and sufficient power, yet delays, grid constraints and inflation can postpone revenue commencements or raise project costs. These pressures may reduce returns on new investment and make growth execution more capital intensive.
